en: Therīgāthā 2.8, Dukanipāta: The Verses of the Nun Abhayamātā I am no longer subject to birth; My rebirth has been eradicated. Having realized the state of peace, I have attained the final Nibbāna. I am no longer subject to death; My life-span has reached its end. Having abandoned all attachments, I have transcended all suffering. I am no longer subject to old age; My youth has passed away. Having attained the state of immortality, I dwell in the bliss of liberation. I am no longer subject to illness; My body is free from disease. Having attained the state of health, I abide in the peace of the Dhamma. I am no longer subject to craving; My thirst for existence is quenched. Having severed the bonds of attachment, I have crossed over the ocean of saṃsāra. I am no longer subject to delusion; My ignorance has been dispelled. Having attained the light of wisdom, I dwell in the radiance of truth. I am no longer subject to fear; My heart is free from trembling. Having attained the state of fearlessness, I abide in the security of Nibbāna. I am no longer subject to grief; My sorrow has come to an end. Having attained the state beyond sorrow, I dwell in the joy of the Dhamma. I am no longer subject to lamentation; My wailing has ceased. Having attained the state of non-lamentation, I abide in the peace of the noble ones. I am no longer subject to despair; My despondency has vanished. Having attained the state of hopefulness, I dwell in the confidence of the Dhamma. I am no longer subject to doubt; My uncertainty has been resolved. Having attained the state of certainty, I abide in the knowledge of the Truth. I am no longer subject to bondage; My fetters have been broken. Having attained the state of freedom, I dwell in the liberation of the mind. I am no longer subject to defilements; My impurities have been washed away. Having attained the state of purity, I abide in the stainlessness of virtue. I am no longer subject to passion; My lust has been extinguished. Having attained the state of dispassion, I dwell in the coolness of peace. I am no longer subject to hatred; My aversion has been abandoned. Having attained the state of loving-kindness, I abide in the compassion of the Buddha. I am no longer subject to ignorance; My blindness has been removed. Having attained the state of clear vision, I dwell in the light of omniscience. Thus, having realized the Dhamma, And having attained the goal, I have fulfilled my purpose; There is nothing further to be done. I pay homage to the Blessed One, The Teacher of the world, Who has shown me the path To the end of suffering. I pay homage to the Sangha, The community of the noble ones, Who have followed the path And attained the fruit of liberation. May this merit be dedicated To the welfare of all beings; May they all attain the peace Of the supreme Nibbāna. Thus spoke the nun Abhayamātā, Having attained the state of arahantship, Free from all fear and sorrow, Abiding in the bliss of the Dhamma.
“From the soles of the feet upward, dear one,
and from the hair at the crown downward—
I have become cool and am extinguished.
… Thus spoke the elder nun Abhayamātā.
